summary: In the car, Neo reluctantly removes his T-shirt and lies back while Trinity seals a device over his navel and Switch plugs it into the cigarette lighter. Trinity explains they think he is bugged and turns a dial so the cylinder sucks hard at his stomach. As the pressure gauge climbs, an ultrasound monitor shows his insides slithering and something wiggling beneath his skin. Switch warns the bug is on the move and that Trinity will lose it, but Trinity refuses and fires an electric charge into Neo, convulsing him until a fluke-like bug rockets out through the extractor's coils. Neo reacts in shock to the thing being real; Trinity lifts the glass cage showing the bug squirming inside, then rolls down the window and dumps it out.

what_changes.before: He does not know what the device is, asking "What is this thing?"
what_changes.after: He learns he is bugged and sees the extracted bug is real, exclaiming "Jesus Christ!  It's real?!"
what_changes.evidence:
NEO

TRINITY

what_changes.after: Subjected to pain and electric current, then relieved of the internal parasite.
what_changes.evidence:
Neo screams, squinting in pain as Trinity watches the
needle on a pressure gauge climb steadily.

what_changes.before: Attempting a non-invasive extraction with the device bearing down on him.
what_changes.after: She escalates to lethal-seeming force, electrocuting Neo to force the bug out.
what_changes.evidence:
TRINITY
No I'm not.  Clear.
The foreboding word hangs in Neo's ear for a moment when
Trinity squeezes a trigger.  Electric current hammers
into Neo

event_hint.one_line: Trinity extracts a tracking bug from Neo's stomach using a specialized device.

minds.wants: To understand what is being done to him and to stop the pain — or at least to survive it.
minds.feels: A terrified, violated bewilderment that escalates into a kind of awe when the abstract idea of a 'bug' becomes a physical, writhing thing. His body is being used as a site of war, and the violation of his own interior slithering beneath his skin is more shocking than the pain itself.
minds.shows: Grudging compliance ('grudgingly strips off his T-shirt'), frightened questions ('What is this thing?'), screams of pain, and finally raw astonishment ('Jesus Christ! It's real?!').
minds.basis: He strips 'grudgingly' (sc-023 he only agreed to cooperate after Trinity's appeal to trust); he asks 'What is this thing?' showing he has no idea what's happening; he screams and squints in pain; his final line is shock at the reality of the bug. The scene notes his knowledge shift from ignorance to knowing he's bugged and seeing the bug is real.

believes_about.belief: That she is hurting him with casual or even malicious intent — that 'Clear' is a threat and the electrocution is an act of cruelty.
believes_about.wrong_because: Trinity's escalation is a desperate medical necessity to dislodge a bug that is 'on the move' and about to be lost; her 'No I'm not' is a refusal to let it escape, not a wish to harm him. Neo cannot yet know her violence is protective.

believes_about.belief: That his body is still simply his own, and that the world he knows operates on ordinary rules.
believes_about.wrong_because: The writhing thing beneath his skin is physical proof that his body has been secretly colonized by technology — the first concrete crack in his understanding of reality, which ev-006 through ev-009 will shatter entirely.

minds.wants: To extract the tracking bug before it burrows deeper and is lost — to protect the crew by removing the wire tap on Neo.
minds.feels: Focused urgency edged with strain; she is performing a high-stakes procedure on an unanesthetized, terrified man and must override both his pain and her own reluctance, escalating to electrocution because the gentler method is failing.
minds.shows: Calm, directive commands ('Lie back,' 'Try to relax,' 'Come on, come on...'), steady monitoring of the pressure gauge, and the clipped, decisive 'Clear' before she fires the current. She shows no outward remorse until after the job is done.
minds.basis: She reassures him to 'relax' while the machine hurts him; mutters 'Come on, come on...' showing pressure to succeed; when Switch warns 'You're gonna lose it,' she refuses ('No I'm not') and immediately escalates to lethal-seeming force. The what_changes notes her shift from non-invasive to electrocution.

believes_about.belief: That he can be managed through reassurance and authority — that 'try to relax' will get him to submit quietly.
believes_about.wrong_because: Neo is not relaxing; he is screaming and terrified, and only survives the procedure by being overpowered. Trinity's faith in calm control is repeatedly undercut by the reality that she must hurt him to save him — a pattern of her having to force what she cannot persuade.

believes_about.belief: That Switch's running commentary ('You're gonna lose it') is unhelpful second-guessing that she must shut down to stay focused.
believes_about.wrong_because: Switch is right — the bug IS on the move and Trinity nearly does lose it, which is exactly why Trinity has to electrocute Neo. Switch isn't undermining her; he's reading the same monitor she is.

minds.wants: To keep the operation on track and prevent the bug from escaping — and, underlying that, to maintain control of a situation that has already gone sideways once (the standoff in sc-023).
minds.feels: A watchful, impatient alertness; he is the one scanning for the failure mode ('It's on the move,' 'You're gonna lose it') while Trinity is locked on the procedure, carrying the residual tension of having held Neo at gunpoint moments before.
minds.shows: Terse technical warnings and a plug snapped into the lighter; he stays in the observer/announcer role rather than acting, deferring the physical decision to Trinity.
minds.basis: In sc-023 Switch was the hard one — gun trained on Neo, 'Our way or the highway,' 'coppertop.' Here he handles the cable and calls out the escalating danger but lets Trinity run the device and make the call to electrocute. His lines are all预警 about losing the bug.

believes_about.belief: That she is about to botch the extraction ('You're gonna lose it') — that her current approach is failing.
believes_about.wrong_because: Trinity does not lose it; she adapts instantly by electrocuting Neo and succeeds. Switch's warning is accurate about the risk but wrong about Trinity's ability to close it — she proves she won't lose it, precisely by doing what he couldn't foresee.

believes_about.belief: That Neo is a 'coppertop' liability — a potential threat to be controlled, as established when he held him at gunpoint.
believes_about.wrong_because: Neo is being cooperatively, if fearfully, subjected to agony for the crew's protection; he is a victim of the same system they're fighting, not an adversary. Switch's hostility (sc-023) misreads Neo's role.

connects_back: sc-023: Neo's coerced compliance — his 'Fine' and grudging agreement to 'try to trust' Trinity is what allows this procedure to happen at all; the gunpoint standoff resolves into this medical violation.
sc-023: Trinity's appeal ('you've been down there... that's not where you want to be') buys the fragile trust she now spends by hurting him.
sc-023: Switch's 'Our way or the highway' posture carries into his watchful, controlling role here.
sets_up: ev-006: The extraction proves Neo's body is a colonized, wired object — the first experiential proof that his reality is false, priming his acceptance of the red pill and unplugging.
ev-006/ev-007: The bug as a physical trace program establishes that the Matrix surveils and marks its inhabitants, foreshadowing how the crew tracks and extracts people.
ev-008: The violation of Neo's body anticipates the discovery of his grafted ports and the horror of his physical modification.
ev-005: Trinity's willingness to hurt Neo to protect the mission sets the tone for the tense, controlled dynamic as she leads him into the Hotel Lafayette.
dramatic_function: The scene converts the abstract paranoia of the chase into undeniable physical fact — Neo's own body betrays him — which is the first irreversible proof that the world he trusted is a lie, and it bonds him to the crew through a shared, painful secret while establishing Trinity as someone who will harm the person she's saving.
